entries.title: Damron-Hanson-Houdré-Xu 2019 Theorem 1: planar quantile separation
entries.statement: For iid nonnegative nearest-neighbor edge weights on Z^2 with distribution F, let I be the infimum of the support. Assume F(0)<p_c for two-dimensional bond percolation and, when I>0, F(I)<the two-dimensional oriented bond threshold. For T(0,x), Theorem 1 supplies thresholds A_x<B_x and constants p,q,c>0 such that, for all sufficiently large ||x||, P(T(0,x)<=A_x)>=p, P(T(0,x)>=B_x)>=q, and B_x-A_x>=c sqrt(log ||x||). The theorem is for the full lattice in dimension two; its higher-dimensional discussion concerns thin cylinders with an additional moment condition. It does not assert an n^(1/3) scale.
assumptions: iid nonnegative edge weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2

entries.title: Two separated quantiles force a sharp variance lower bound
entries.statement: Let X be a square-integrable real random variable. If a<b, p,q>0, P(X<=a)>=p and P(X>=b)>=q, then Var(X)>=pq(b-a)^2/(p+q). The constant is sharp for fixed p and q.
entries.proof_text: The two events are disjoint, so p+q<=1. Put mu=E X. If a<=mu<=b, integrate the squared deviation on the two events and minimize p(mu-a)^2+q(b-mu)^2 over mu; its minimum is pq(b-a)^2/(p+q). If mu<a or mu>b, the opposite tail alone gives at least q(b-a)^2 or p(b-a)^2, which is stronger. Equality is attained by masses p at a, q at b, and 1-p-q at (pa+qb)/(p+q); this law has that middle point as its mean.

entries.title: Planar FPP quantile separation implies logarithmic variance lower bound
entries.statement: Under Damron-Hanson-Houdré-Xu 2019 Theorem 1's exact Z^2 edge-law assumptions, its two fixed-probability quantiles separated by c sqrt(log ||x||) imply Var(T(0,x))>=c' log ||x|| whenever T(0,x) is square-integrable. This corrects the categorical claim that quantitative interval anti-concentration cannot itself lower-bound variance. The conclusion is logarithmic and leaves the P0104 subdiffusive/KPZ exponent target untouched.
assumptions: T(0,x) square-integrable for the variance conclusion

relations.rationale: The source theorem gives the two positive-probability tails and sqrt(log ||x||) separation used by the corollary.
The abstract lemma turns the source theorem's two tail probabilities and their separation into a variance lower bound.
The corollary yields only c log n, while the existing P0104 card asks for a power-law exponent below 1/2 and planar chi=1/3; this is background lower-bound context, not a solution.
